## Edge Dominating Set on general graphs

ID: `edge-dominating-set-budget`

Track: `fpt`

Claim status: `not-obtained-by-this-route`; review: `ai-audited`

**Parameter.** Selected-edge budget k, with no maximum-degree or sparsity restriction

**Obstacle for this route.** The explicit Xiao–Kloks–Poon kernel used for this route has at most 2k²+2k vertices and O(k³) edges. The shared endpoint-OR encoding uses one variable per remaining edge, plus O(m′) auxiliary variables, so its guarantee is N+M = O(k³), not O(k). Substituting into the sparse SAT bound gives only $2^{O(k^3/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}$; it does not establish a subexponential-in-k consequence. Having a VC of size at most 2k is only necessary for EDS of size at most k: two disjoint edges with k=1 are a counterexample to the converse. The guarantees of ordinary VC kernelization do not by themselves justify fixing the same vertices as mandatory endpoints for Edge Dominating Set. On the path a-b-c-d, {a,c} and {b,c} are both minimum vertex covers, but requiring {a,c} to be endpoints needs two selected edges, whereas the single edge bc dominates the graph. Section 2 of the source explains the additional matching step after a cover is fixed.

**Next step.** Seek a fixed-width CNF with O(k) total Boolean variables, including the witness/verification of edge pairing, or a different reduction that preserves EDS. Polynomial-time matching verification alone gives no linear-variable bound. This records the limitation of one explicit kernel/encoding route, not a lower bound, an impossibility result, or a latest-best kernel claim. The general-m exact entry and fixed-maximum-degree FPT entry are separate positive consequences.

**Sources.**

- **`xiao-kloks-poon2011`** — [Mingyu Xiao, Ton Kloks, and Sheung-Hung Poon, New Parameterized Algorithms for Edge Dominating Set](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1104.4160v1). Version: arXiv:1104.4160v1, 21 April 2011; 18-page preprint. Locator: Section 2, printed page 2 (matching after choosing a minimal vertex cover); Section 6, Lemma 9, printed page 11 (2k²+2k vertices and O(k³) edges).

## Cluster Editing

ID: `cluster-editing-budget`

Track: `fpt`

Claim status: `not-obtained-by-this-route`; review: `draft`

**Parameter.** Edge-edit budget k

**Obstacle for this route.** A linear-vertex kernel still leaves quadratically many potential edge choices in the natural encoding. This route does not establish O(k) Boolean variables.

**Next step.** Investigate whether a representation with sufficiently few variables exists; distinguish weighted and unweighted kernel outputs.

**Sources.**

- **`cluster-editing2010`** — [Yixin Cao and Jianer Chen, Cluster Editing: Kernelization based on Edge Cuts](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.4250v3). Version: arXiv:1008.4250v3, 10 September 2010. Locator: Abstract and kernel statement.

Track: `fpt`

Claim status: `candidate`; review: `draft`

**Parameter.** Vertex cover number or cograph-deletion number k

**Obstacle for this route.** Eliminating outside vertices preserves existence of an extension but discards the number of extensions. Counting the boundary CNF gives the wrong quantity in general.

## Dense 0–1 Permanent

ID: `exact-dense-permanent-vertex-measure`

Track: `exact`

Claim status: `not-obtained-by-this-route`; review: `draft`

**Size measure.** Matrix dimension n, not the number m of nonzero entries

**Obstacle for this route.** The edge-variable encoding gives B(m); at $m=\Theta(n^2)$ its guarantee is $2^{O(n^2/\sqrt{\log n})}$, which does not improve the classical vertex/dimension-exponential benchmark.

**Next step.** Investigate a representation handling dense linear factors without paying for all matrix incidences. Treat any stronger algebraic theorem as a separate assumption profile.

## Hamiltonian Cycle, especially sparse graphs

ID: `exact-hamiltonian-cycle-vertex-measure`

Track: `exact`

Claim status: `candidate`; review: `draft`

**Size measure.** Number n of vertices; separately record m edges

**Obstacle for this route.** Local degree-two constraints count 2-factors, which need not be connected. The earlier Cut&Count idea requires an algebraic counting routine beyond the current SAT profiles, including weight and coefficient bit complexity.

**Next step.** Audit the manuscript’s general algebra routine as a separate profile. In particular, a polynomial ring of degree O(m²) cannot simply be assumed to satisfy the linear truncation bound of the tensor theorem. Track randomness and isolate the connectivity step.

Claim status: `candidate`; review: `draft`

**Size measure.** Number n of vertices, with weight bit length tracked separately

**Obstacle for this route.** Besides connectivity, a weight-generating polynomial can have degree depending on numerical weight values, rather than their bit length. The local degree-constraint counting entry does not resolve either issue.
